Henry again tries to control him through the diagnosis of Huntington's disease and invents the possibility of a new treatment. Baxter orders Daisy to read from her book. Instead she recites Matthew Arnold's poem about love and uncertainty; Baxter, believing it is hers, is unexpectedly absorbed and asks to hear more. The change gives Henry and Theo an opening. They attack, and Baxter falls down the stairs, sustaining a serious head injury, while Nigel flees. An ambulance takes Baxter to the hospital. The immediate threat is over, but Henry knows the injured man will require the kind of specialist care that Henry himself can provide.

Henry goes to the hospital and joins Jay Strauss in operating on Baxter's damaged brain. He sets aside anger over the invasion and concentrates on saving the patient, finding in surgery a precise moral task after a day dominated by political uncertainty and random danger. Baxter survives the operation and will face both his injury, possible prosecution, and the progression of Huntington's disease. Henry returns home near dawn. Daisy's pregnancy is now openly known, and the family's ordeal has reinforced their attachment to one another. He finds Rosalind awake, and the couple reconnect before he finally prepares to sleep. The Saturday closes where it began, in their bedroom, but Henry can no longer regard the security of his professional and domestic life as something guaranteed. He can protect and repair only what comes within reach, and on this night that has meant preserving the life of the man who threatened him.

characters.description: The void-using leader of a nine-person party newly arrived in Savannah. Derek seeks property for a combined home and business while pursuing a meeting with the city's ruling house.
characters.name: Derek Hunt

characters.description: Derek's telepathic companion and a member of his traveling household. She registers alongside the group when they enter Savannah.
characters.name: Silvi

characters.description: A member of Derek's party who enters Savannah and publicly declares that House Torith no longer binds him. A former associate recognizes him as Jackson and the Crimson Blade.
characters.name: Jacks

characters.description: A contract specialist traveling with Derek's household. He arrives in Savannah as part of the group that needs permanent accommodation and commercial premises.
characters.name: Rudy

characters.description: A wind user who arrives in Savannah among the people under Derek's protection. She is part of the household seeking a stable new base in the city.
characters.name: Rayna West

characters.description: A young crafter who reaches Savannah with her mother, Malorie, and Derek's group. The party's search for a permanent home also needs room for her developing work.
characters.name: Brandi Fields

characters.description: Brandi's mother and a member of Derek's newly arrived household. She enters Savannah with the group as they move into temporary Crown lodging.
characters.name: Malorie

characters.description: A young spear trainee traveling under Derek's protection. He arrives with the household that plans to settle in Savannah and prepare him for further training.
characters.name: Thomas Stewart

characters.description: A Crown manager and Derek's commercial contact in Savannah. She covers the party's entry charge against future proceeds and directs him toward finding property while Alanah Swan arranges discounted temporary lodging.
characters.name: Stella Brighton

characters.description: The Crown leader whose arrangements secure reduced-price hotel rooms for Derek's party. Her support gives the newcomers a temporary base while they establish themselves in Savannah.
characters.name: Alanah Swan

characters.description: The head of House Savannah and the city leader Derek hopes to meet. Access to her requires an appointment, so he first turns his attention to securing property.
characters.name: Natalie Savannah

characters.description: Savannah's Onyx-ranked Adventurer's Guildmaster and an expert spear user. After assessing Thomas's promise, he grants the trainee unrestricted access to a high-tier room and offers regular instruction.
characters.name: Shae

characters.description: Derek reports killing this son after hearing him acknowledge a role in trafficking children. The admission is Derek's only evidence, and he believes the man had limited knowledge of the broader operation.
characters.name: Gerald Torith's son

characters.description: An Indrian elf dignitary, the daughter of a duke and niece of her kingdom's ruler. She encounters Derek at the Guild with an earlier hostile exchange between them still unsettled.
characters.name: Sabrina Elris

characters.description: The short, stout proprietor of the bar where Shae brings Derek after his rank assessment. Shae introduces the two men over a celebratory drink.
characters.name: Roman

characters.description: The Alabaster Homes representative competing to construct Derek's mixed residence and business. He distinguishes his bid by offering to complete the project at the cost of materials.
characters.name: Jeffrey

characters.description: Roman's research assistant, an alchemist specializing in research and herbology. She observes Derek's experimental potion tests at Roman's shop.
characters.name: Freya

characters.description: Sidaria's king, confronted with Gerald's allegations against Derek and Alanah's account of the kidnapping of Brandi and Malorie. He promises an independent inquiry into the dispute.
characters.name: King Edwin

characters.description: The Sidarian crown prince, present when Alanah presents her account of Derek's conflict with House Torith. He shows an immediate interest in meeting the newly ranked adventurer.
characters.name: Edward

characters.description: A powerful House Torith noble who accuses Derek of killing members of his family and guards. He denies knowledge of the kidnapping attributed to his son and faces a royal inquiry.
characters.name: Gerald Torith

characters.description: Gerald Torith's dead son, named among the people Gerald accuses Derek of killing. Gerald claims Malcolm acted without his knowledge in the kidnapping attributed to him.
characters.name: Malcolm

characters.description: A Crown figure who oversees two of Alanah Swan's students while preparations begin for the Savannah void-beast auction.
characters.name: Avery Swan

characters.description: A platinum-ranked academy graduate serving in Edgar's military company and adventuring party. He comes to Derek's shop after receiving a letter from his father, Jacks.
characters.name: Jake Herrett

characters.description: An Onyx adventurer, military leader, and Jake's superior. He accompanies Jake to Savannah, then joins the urgent effort to rescue Jacks from an ambush outside the city.
characters.name: Edgar

characters.description: A returning House Torith criminal already confined by Derek when the book begins. His continued custody is part of the unresolved conflict between Derek's group and House Torith.
characters.name: Clay Torith

characters.description: An armored protector traveling with Gerald Torith. He is next in line to a noble family ranked third in power within the kingdom and accompanies Gerald to a covert meeting beyond the capital.
characters.name: Gerald Torith's armored bodyguard

characters.description: The first son of House Arden and a formidable earth user. He helps Gerald ambush Edward's party in the palace courtyard and attacks the prince's guards.
characters.name: Cliff Arden

characters.description: The shadow-using vice leader of the Assassin's Guild who joins Gerald's palace ambush. This attacker restrains and grievously injures Edward's guards while delaying the crown prince.
characters.name: Assassin's Guild vice leader

characters.description: A cloaked ally of Gerald who participates in the palace ambush using plant-based attacks. The attack leaves his identity concealed when he first joins the fighting.
characters.name: Unidentified plant user

characters.description: The House Arden heir whom Edgar identifies as the earth user Cliff Arden. He is one of Gerald's allies inside the shadow-sealed battlefield.
characters.name: Clifford Arden

characters.description: The shadow-using Assassin's Guild vice leader, now identified by Edgar. Her abilities have sealed the battlefield and disabled Edward while Gerald's group attempts to escape.
characters.name: Vanessa Hodges

recaps.ending: Derek's household is established in its Savannah shop-home: Brandi crafts with Crown support, Malorie manages the business, Rudy handles contracts, Thomas prepares for the academy, and Rayna has reached level 100 with Zephyr's Fury. Derek returns from the Golem Dungeon at level 171 with unexplained points beyond the apparent endurance and vitality cap. His experiment with Clay also shows that Time Prison can devastate a human captive's will. Natalie Savannah and King Edwin accept Derek's case against Gerald, but Gerald uses concealed allies and teleportation routes to evade arrest. His party ambushes Edward, kills palace guards, and severs the prince's arms. Avery delays the escape until Derek and Edgar arrive. Edward survives and has his arms restored, while Derek's side captures Gerald, Clifford Arden, Vanessa Hodges, and an unidentified half-elf plant user. They return to Savannah with all four held in Time Prison. Gerald's Indrian contacts, captives, teleportation network, and raid-team informant remain unresolved. Edgar is still assembling the expedition into the severely time-distorted level-250 dungeon.
recaps.in_short: Derek Hunt settles his companions in Savannah, earns Onyx rank, and turns a leased lot into a shared home, forge, shop, and contract business. Roman begins training Brandi and partners with Derek on permanent-stat potions made from void-beast materials. Jacks trains Rayna to level 100 and reconciles with his son Jake after surviving an ambush. Derek then spends two weeks mastering the Golem Dungeon, reaches level 171, and discovers both an unexplained stat-cap anomaly and the severe human cost of Time Prison. As the Crown prepares a dangerous time-distorted raid, Natalie Savannah and King Edwin move against Gerald Torith. Gerald escapes through a hidden network and ambushes Edward's detention force. Avery holds the attackers until Derek and Edgar arrive. Edward survives with restored arms, and Gerald, Clifford Arden, Vanessa Hodges, and an unidentified plant user are captured in Time Prison and taken to Savannah, leaving Gerald's wider conspiracy and the coming raid unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Derek Hunt leads a group that includes Silvi, Jacks, Rudy, Rayna West, Brandi Fields, Malorie, and Thomas Stewart. He has commercial ties to the Crown through Alanah Swan and Stella Brighton. Conflict with House Torith remains active. Clay Torith is already Derek's prisoner, and Derek's companions have previously suffered retaliation connected to the house. Derek also possesses void-based abilities and has an arrangement involving valuable void beasts. As the group enters a new stage of its journey, its immediate priorities are safety, stable work, and a defensible home.

Derek and eight companions enter Savannah, where Stella Brighton places them in temporary rooms at the Crown Hotel. Derek leases a vacant commercial lot for a combined residence, workshop, store, and contract service. Jacks, newly free of House Torith, writes to the adult son he kept distant while bound to the house. Coffee and stimulant revenue from the Crown gives Derek enough money to begin building plans and open a local bank account. Thomas independently visits the Adventurer's Guild and impresses Guildmaster Shae, an Onyx-ranked spear expert who offers him demanding instruction ahead of academy enrollment. Derek then seeks his own promotion from Gold to Onyx. His aura overwhelms the Guild's testing equipment, bringing Shae into the assessment. Their spar reveals Derek's exceptional durability, healing, lightning, and unusual movement. Shae agrees to keep Derek's abilities confidential, judges him qualified for Onyx, and learns Derek's account of killing Gerald Torith's son after an admission connected to child trafficking. Derek lacks proof of the wider operation, but his rank assessment is complete.

Derek receives his Onyx badge and meets Sabrina Elris, an Indrian dignitary with whom he has unresolved hostility. Shae introduces him to Roman, a halfling alchemist whose bar supports his experimental work. Derek agrees to test unknown potions in exchange for Roman giving Brandi serious alchemy instruction. Meanwhile, Derek defines roles for his Savannah household: Rudy will handle contracts, Brandi will develop her crafts, Malorie will support the home and business, Jacks will guard and train Rayna, and Thomas will continue with Shae. Derek selects building materials and solicits rapid construction bids. Jeffrey of Alabaster Homes offers to build at material cost because cultivating goodwill with an Onyx adventurer is valuable, and Rudy completes the contract. At Roman's shop, Brandi begins basic potion work. Derek survives three dangerous experimental brews: one causes catastrophic internal injury, another produces temporary petrification, and the last permanently raises four physical attributes. Roman indicates that the successful potion used void-beast material, creating the basis for a larger partnership.

Derek and Roman agree to produce permanent physical-stat potions from Derek's expected void-beast materials, with Derek receiving the strongest results and sharing profits from the rest. Jacks takes Rayna through severe accelerated training meant to replace her dependence on rescue with practical survival ability. Jeffrey finishes Derek's two-story shop-home, including Brandi's forge, Rudy's contract space, living quarters, and a large kitchen, then partners with Derek on a rune-powered shower design. At court, Alanah Swan announces the Crown's coming void-beast auctions and challenges Gerald Torith's accusations against Derek. King Edwin agrees to investigate after hearing about the kidnapping of Brandi and Malorie. Jake Herrett arrives with Edgar after receiving Jacks's letter, but Rayna soon reports that Jacks has been ambushed outside Savannah. Derek, Edgar, and Jake rescue him and capture twelve half-elf attackers. Questioning shows that the attackers acted on their own in hopes of pleasing Sabrina Elris, not on proven orders from her. Jacks and Jake reconcile. Jacks shares his unproven belief that House Torith engineered Jake's childhood abduction and his wife's murder to bind him, and father and son agree that the house must eventually face accountability.

Rayna reaches level 100 and upgrades into Zephyr's Fury, an epic ranged wind-swordsman class, then earns a Gold Guild badge. Malorie takes charge of the shop, Roman receives void-beast ingredients for his potion work, and the Crown considers auctioning the first Potion of Physical Permanence. Derek leaves alone for the level-170 Golem Dungeon. Elsewhere, an unstable level-250 raid dungeon with extreme time distortion forces the royal family to choose Edgar to lead a twenty-five-person expedition. Derek repeatedly clears elemental golem encounters, using their attacks for resistance training and learning how to preserve valuable mana cores. He completes the dungeon, re-enters for an intensive two-week training block, and accumulates levels and skill improvements. The Crown combines its auctions into one large Savannah event before the raid, and Stella confirms that Roman's potion grants permanent physical gains. Edgar is rapidly raised toward level 250 while insisting on selecting a capable, trusted expedition team. By the end of Derek's training block, he has reached level 165 and raised endurance and vitality to the apparent system cap of 1,500. Five additional points in each disappear behind question marks, leaving their effect unknown.

Derek gathers more than thirty Void Beast carcasses and tests Time Prison inside the Golem Dungeon. Clay Torith completes an accelerated sentence but emerges terrified of renewed confinement and deliberately enters a golem's fatal attack. Derek concludes that the prison can rapidly destroy a human captive's will and restricts its acceptable use to the gravest cases. Edgar reaches level 250 with a concealed wisdom-based legendary class and begins choosing volunteers for the time-distorted raid. Derek finishes training at level 171 and returns to Savannah. Brandi has reached level 27, gained an epic class, and expanded her crafting skills, while Malorie supervises her safety. Derek finally meets Alanah in person, demonstrates resistance to her abilities, and discloses his void powers and large stockpile. The Crown accepts most of his Void Beast bodies, offers confidential support for Brandi, and explains that his excess stat points lie beyond the system's calculable cap. At a pre-auction dinner, Natalie Savannah verifies Derek's account against Gerald. She bars Gerald's immediate family from Savannah trade and entry, while King Edwin resolves to imprison him. The move comes too late for an immediate arrest because Gerald has already left the palace.

Gerald meets Indrian contacts at a hidden warehouse where people are held in cages. He has concealed teleportation routes, an informant among the selected raid force, and a plan to seize control of Sidaria. Although Natalie offers to hold him in Savannah and investigate his oaths and network, Gerald evades the first attempt to detain him. Edward returns to the capital to make the arrest, only to be ambushed by Gerald, Clifford Arden, an unidentified half-elf plant user, and shadow specialist Vanessa Hodges. Guards are killed, Edward loses both arms, and Avery Swan intervenes alone to prevent the attackers from escaping. Alanah sends Derek and Edgar through a private teleportation circle as reinforcements. They breach Vanessa's shadow barrier after Avery has exhausted much of his stamina holding the group. Derek incapacitates Gerald and confines him in Time Prison, then defeats Clifford without killing him. Avery overcomes the plant user, rescues one surviving guard, and helps Edward recover and reattach his arms. Edgar defeats Vanessa and takes her apparent storage devices. Gerald, Clifford, Vanessa, and the plant user are all placed in Time Prison, and the victors return to Savannah with the prisoners. Gerald's broader network and the impending time-distorted raid remain open threats.

characters.description: The book's viewpoint character, a first-year crafter-appraiser at Quest Academy recovering from the injuries of his reclaimed-zone excursion. His silver eyes appraise any object in exact detail, and his fused Mythcrafter ability builds extraordinary gear from powers he has copied with Skill Master. Ranked third in his year, he still shuns front-line combat, set instead on founding a crafting guild that could lift many heroes at once.
characters.name: Salvatore "Sal" Argento

characters.description: Daughter of the telepath Nero and one of the Academy's highest-ranked first-years, a mind-control specialist who can compel others and read surface thoughts. Named captain of Sal's tower team, she is made to wear an ability-suppressing locket for the entire trial as punishment for harming him during the excursion. Cold and controlling, she treats teammates as pieces to be positioned rather than people to trust.
characters.name: Erika Clifton

characters.description: An offense-class member of Sal's team, secretly the vanished child hero Gallant. His original power evolved at his lowest point into a volatile, trauma-fueled ability that a restraining locket keeps suppressed rather than healed. Sal has taken on the personal project of crafting a way to give him true mastery over it. Gifted and charming in public, he is colder and more dangerous underneath.
characters.name: Brophy

characters.description: Sal's crafting mentor and the workshop's lead lecturer, known by her hero alias, whose ability turns her gear into powered mechanical armor. Warm but exacting, she funds and co-builds his commissions, reins in his habit of taking on too much at once, and helps set up a machine that lets him test skill weaves safely outside a living body.
characters.name: Upgrade

characters.description: The headmaster of Quest Academy, who goes by a chosen name. His "system" ability reads and quantifies essence and keeps a vast searchable log of the Academy's activity. A merit-focused mentor with a personal stake in Sal, he negotiates the terms on which Sal may use his power to improve other people's abilities, while shielding him from outside guild and Hunter Bureau pressure.
characters.name: Quest

characters.description: A first-year crafting classmate and one of Sal's steadiest friends, a gifted tailor with a construct ability and a hardened, reclaimed-zone upbringing. Modest about her own talent, she collaborates on the team's gear while rapidly closing the gap with Sal's own work, and is determined to earn a place among the Academy's best on her own merit rather than through friendship.
characters.name: Blathnaid McClean

characters.description: A foresight-gifted first-year and Sal's closest confidant, whose eyes turn white when she reads possible futures. Candid and fiercely loyal, she works quietly for a disaster-prevention circle and often glimpses trouble before it arrives. She tries to steer Sal away from his worst possible futures while deliberately refusing to spoil the good ones.
characters.name: Divinity Khan

characters.description: A first-year healer on Sal's team whose Transference ability drains essence from one target to mend another. Once ostracized for trying to charge for healing, she is a warm, sharp ally with a deep, self-taught grasp of essence theory. She is being fitted with a powerful crafted coat meant to fix her chronic shortage of usable essence.
characters.name: Rochelle de Verdon

characters.description: A student alchemist who sells homemade tonics and elixirs from a market stall. Shrewd and playful, he brews everything from insight-surfacing draughts to mastery boosters, and strikes a supply deal with Sal, trading elixir work for rare portal-sourced ingredients routed through the Argento auction house.
characters.name: Alex

characters.description: A first-year body manipulator and already a ranked hunter, introduced when he brings Sal and Blathnaid on a scavenger run. His ability reshapes his own muscle for enormous leaping strength and speed. Gruff and insecure about his place among Sal's friends, he is plainly devoted to Blathnaid, covering her fees and giving away most of his earnings for her sake.
characters.name: Darren

characters.description: A guarded third-year Savior-class student whose Nullify ability severs a target's essence, lethal to demons but backlashing painfully on her with each use. Sharp and hard to read, she is being courted by several guilds at once. Sal targets her as a recruit for his own future guild, winning her interest only after an attempt at manipulation fails and he honestly improves her real ability.
characters.name: Anna Sakura

characters.description: A low-ranked illusionist and one of Sal's closest friends, sharp-tongued and inventive. His illusions form decoys, invisibility, and full training scenarios, and he takes quickly to a crafted gear set that lets him hide real conjured blades among fakes. Quietly top of every academic subject, he needles Sal constantly while pushing him to stand up for the overlooked.
characters.name: Barry Francis

characters.description: The defense-class member of Sal's team, a large, soft-spoken warder whose rune barriers shield the group. Quiet and unassuming where his teammates are loud, he is one of the steadier hands on a fractious team, more at ease building protective wards than drawing attention to himself.
characters.name: The Team's Warder

characters.description: A top-ranked Hunter Bureau hero and Gallant's mother, who guides Sal's team through the tower trial. Poised, exacting, and immensely powerful, she runs the trial as a strict graded exercise of escalating handicaps and hidden objectives. She has spent years seeking a specialist to treat her son's condition, and sees far more in Sal than he admits to being.
characters.name: Prestige

characters.description: A Hunter Bureau researcher who holds the rare Skill Savant ability, able to grant powers of his own creation into others for a time. He runs the synchronization analysis behind every weave Sal submits to the workshop's simulation machine, and takes an intense professional interest once Sal's results begin exceeding what anyone thought possible.
characters.name: Grant

characters.description: A relaxed, formidable hunter the team rescues partway through the tower trial. Recognizing the Argento and Clifton family names, he offers to keep assisting them through the harder floors and takes an easy, obvious enjoyment in real danger. There is plainly far more to him than a rescued hunter, though he keeps it to himself for now.
characters.name: Rob

characters.description: A credit-floor broker and one of Sal's most determined advocates, tied to the Reavers Guild and set on founding a guild alongside him one day. Her body-manipulation ability forces essence gates open far faster than natural growth allows. Transactional and protective, she manages his materials and sales and pushes his ambitions past what he would attempt alone.
characters.name: Vanessa

recaps.ending: Book 3 ends with Quest Academy's first Savior class seated and the Tower trial resolved. Sal's five-person team survived the trial's genuine floor-five demon incursion without lasting injury. Three of them, plus his close friends Divinity Khan and Barry Francis, are among the first fifteen named Saviors; Gallant and the team's warder are excluded, Gallant for his battle-frenzy breakdown and insubordination, the warder for achievements judged team-carried rather than individual, though both are promised consolation rewards. Sal is named not just a Savior but the single top-ranked Savior in the entire Academy, publicly credited for killing a hulker and for his crafting and skill-implant work. No one dies on-page; the darkest note is a possible sixty-years future Sal glimpses through Divinity's amplified foresight, in which humanity is winning the war but most of the current cast, including his mentor Upgrade, has died, a future Divinity insists remains changeable. Sal's guild ambition advances but is not resolved: with top-Savior status, proof of his hulker kill, and Quest's offer to endorse him at an upcoming gala, he chooses to spend the break at his family's auction house to win his parents' backing in person, the outcome unknown. Rob's demand to take Gallant away, Prestige's alternative, a scheduled meeting with the Ark guildmaster, an outing to the proficiency-holder Coach, Sal's promised reconciliation with Hannah, and the antagonist faction Bastion all remain open, carried into the next book, Legacies.
recaps.in_short: Recovered from his excursion injuries, Sal Argento spends the run-up to a Tower trial winning the headmaster's permission to use his ability to improve other people's powers, chasing a fix for the volatile hidden hero Gallant, and quietly arming his team. Along the way he accidentally creates Perfect, a flawless self-improving ability best suited to himself, which sharpens his crafting, movement, and combat and rapidly grows his power. The Tower turns out to be a staged Hunter Bureau training site that escalates into a genuine demon incursion, where Sal kills his first hulker in melee, Gallant breaks down and is benched, and the team becomes the first to clear five floors. A rescued hunter is revealed as the Bureau's president, who has been watching Sal for months. The Academy then names its first Saviors, and Sal is announced as the single top-ranked Savior in the whole school. He also glimpses a possible sixty-years future in which humanity is winning the war but his mentor has died, and heads home for the break to win his parents' backing for the crafting guild he still means to found.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Quest Academy series: Sal Argento, a guarded young man whose silver eyes appraise any object and who can copy other people's abilities, enrolled at Quest Academy, where heroes train to reclaim demon-held land. During skill registration he accidentally fused several powers into a unique top-tier crafting ability the Academy calls Mythcrafter, and became the protege of the crafting lecturer Upgrade. Befriending the foresight-gifted Divinity Khan, he was drawn into a secret disaster-prevention circle, helped expose Bastion, a wealthy faction seeding loyal students through the Academy, and led a squad of underdogs to victory in the first-year tournament, finishing third overall behind Divinity and Nero's daughter, Erika Clifton. In his second month a harsh new curriculum placed him on Erika's fractious excursion team alongside the healer Rochelle de Verdon, a quiet warder, and an offense cadet secretly the vanished child hero Gallant, whose volatile ability a locket keeps suppressed. Their guardian was the top hero Prestige, revealed to be Gallant's mother. The team passed the reclaimed-zone excursion two wins to one, but Erika twice seized control of Sal's body without consent, once marching him unarmed into stone golems and leaving him with shattered arms and broken ribs. Sal accepted that he had been avoiding real growth, resolved to pursue it as the founder of a crafting guild rather than a frontline fighter, and agreed to try to craft a cure for Gallant's condition, ahead of a looming Tower trial where Prestige expects five cleared floors.

So far this book: recovered from his excursion injuries, Sal negotiates with the headmaster, Quest, for permission to use his ability on consenting people, agreeing to prove himself by producing a set of flawless skill weaves on a new simulation machine that lets him test powers safely outside a living body. Erika is punished for harming him with a locket that will suppress her mind control for the whole coming Tower trial. Wanting to help the volatile Gallant master his suppressed ability, Sal takes that on as a personal goal. Working with Upgrade, he pours enormous effort into a support student whose ability had never functioned, rebuilding it from the ground up and eventually giving her a full, four-stage ability chain, an all but unheard-of result. Quest, wary of the attention Sal's true scope will attract, sets limits and asks him to practice on people with little to lose. Sal also begins researching an ability for himself and for Gallant, and quietly commissions crafted gear for his teammates ahead of the trial. As the stretch closes, an out-of-context message from Divinity, still away on her own excursion, hints that she already knows about work Sal thought was private.

Sal keeps grinding through the simulation machine, improving dozens of students' abilities and earning steady Academy pay for each success, while researching candidate powers to give Gallant true mastery and to build an implant for himself. A session with the Academy's blunt resilience instructor reframes everything: shown hard numbers, Sal accepts he can never personally fix every hero, and that the scalable version of his ambition is to found and lead a guild rather than work alone. He commits firmly to that path. Along the way he reconciles with a group of workshop students he had clashed with, and strikes a supply deal with the student alchemist Alex to source rare ingredients through his family's auction house. Experimenting with combining powers, he concludes his own copying ability may be the binding element that lets several abilities fuse into one. Blathnaid invites him along on a scavenger run into the reclaimed zone with the body manipulator Darren to gather crafting materials, and he accepts.

The scavenger run becomes a self-contained adventure. Guided by the brusque network official Matron, Sal, Blathnaid, and Darren race to the far edge of a picked-over zone, harvest prowler materials, and turn up a cache of lockboxes that may have been a rival team's planted stash. Sal, in his element as a trader raised in an auction house, negotiates their haul for far more than expected, and the trio bank a large sum. Darren, gruff and insecure about his place in the group, tries to give nearly all his earnings to Blathnaid, whom he plainly favors, before the team settles the split more fairly. All three rise sharply in scavenger rank, earning rare recommendations for a first run. Blathnaid shows hardened, reclaimed-zone survival skills alongside her crafting, and the run cements Darren as a genuine friend rather than a reluctant guide. They return to the workshop with a stockpile of premium materials for the coming trial.

Back in the workshop, Sal experiments further with fusing powers and, almost by accident, creates a brand-new ability that summons essence constructs across a wide area, though he cannot use it himself. He finishes a legendary-grade coat for Rochelle, built with Upgrade and Blathnaid, that should fix her chronic essence shortage. He also meets the guarded third-year Anna Sakura, honestly improving her real ability to win her interest in his future guild after an attempt at manipulation backfires. As the month-long excursion ends, the whole first year streams back to the Academy, and a mandatory assembly lays out the semester's structure: a final trial clearing a floor of a demon-filled tower, preceded by mandatory demon-behavior classes, with a licensing track offered as an exit for struggling supports. The visiting lecturer Chatfield announces that roughly three hundred students have been cut from tower eligibility on their excursion results, sharpening the divide between his results-first philosophy and Quest's gentler one. Sal's team, already rested, is among the first scheduled to enter the tower.

The surviving first-years file into mandatory demonic-behavior and tactics classes taught by new professors, learning a full taxonomy of demon types and how to read their behavior. Barry, revealed to be quietly brilliant, shines in the analysis lessons, and Sal equips him with a powerful crafted armor set that hides real conjured blades among illusions. A serious rift opens between Sal and Divinity: with his consent, she discloses a possible future in which following Erika's advice to build a combat ability by copying every hero he meets eventually destroys his eyesight, since his crafting ability already strains beyond his capacity and his eyes have quietly been protected by outside healing all along. Sal refuses to promise he will never take that path, upsetting her. He also spends heavily at a student market, buying an unfinished flight rig he privately imagines completing one day for Divinity. The classes build toward hands-on demon dissection and, beyond it, the tower itself.

During the dissection labs, Gallant shows unexpected patience and expertise as a teacher, while Barry deliberately provokes a public argument with him as a calculated tactic to keep Gallant seeking Sal's favor, warning Sal privately that Gallant's underlying menace is real. Sal and Blathnaid quietly amass a large stockpile of salvaged materials with a professor's blessing. Chasing a mastery ability for Gallant, Sal mistypes a database search and accidentally combines three powers into something entirely new. The result draws the Academy's leadership: Quest, Upgrade, and the researcher Grant, who holds a rare ability-granting power and secretly runs the analysis behind all of Sal's work, pull him from class, and Prestige steps through a teleportation gate to join them. The new ability is named Perfect, a body-manipulation power that continuously improves both learning and existing skills, with hundreds of compatible users including Gallant. They ask Sal to activate it on himself so it can be studied directly.

Sal activates Perfect, and it proves extraordinary: it amplifies a simple health elixir into a full-body restoration that unlocks his essence gates outright, and is confirmed to be a genuinely flawless ability, best suited to Sal himself. Over the following days he drinks a course of elixirs, raising his gate count sharply, while Perfect quietly sharpens his crafting, movement, and technique. Prestige, over Quest's insistence that Gallant must earn his place rather than have it bought, agrees a plan to fix Gallant with Perfect plus an elixir. Quest reveals the party he has trusted to back Sal's guild without exploiting him is Sal's own family's auction house. As the tower nears, Sal freehands a signature gear piece in a crafting flow state, delivers legendary and unique gear to his fully uniformed team, and accepts a sincere apology from Gallant, who has learned Sal broke the rules to help him. The team reaches the tower entrance ready to begin.

The tower proves not to be the peaceful district the cohort walked through but a facility reached by teleportation gate, with Prestige guiding the team and demanding five cleared floors. The first floor is a pitch-dark maze; the team splits, and Sal, Gallant, and Rochelle clear it with rapid revolver work and melee, Rochelle emerging as a genuinely dangerous fighter with her coat's grappling hooks and even soloing the floor's boss. Sal confirms Perfect is boosting his balance, reflexes, and instinct in combat, not only his crafting. Examining the boss, he realizes the whole tower is a staged Hunter Bureau training site stocked with planted demons rather than a real dungeon, something Gallant already knew. Prestige delivers a positive verdict and reveals the run's real format: per-floor handicaps that sideline different members and optional hidden objectives, escalating the challenge as they climb.

The trial climbs through cleverly designed floors, each benching different members. On a platform course, Sal and a locket-restrained Erika find a surprisingly cooperative rhythm, and Sal discovers that Perfect can passively absorb a teammate's ability used on him: a burst of Rochelle's healing essence is redirected into wholesale physical enhancement of his body. On a laboratory floor watched from a balcony, Prestige probes Erika's guarded, tool-like philosophy of leadership, all but confirms her hidden telepathy and a chess-themed hero name, and offers to personally teach Sal a hunter's essence-sensing technique. Gallant displays elite, brutal unarmed combat that Prestige says no veteran has bettered. Several hunters are rescued along the way, including an easygoing one named Rob who offers to keep helping. As the floors end, Prestige reveals that the fourth floor leads directly and irreversibly into the fifth, a point of no return, and sends only Gallant, Sal, and Erika in.

The fourth floor is a running battle up a stairway maze that flows straight into the fifth: a derelict high-rise at the true edge of the demon-held red zone, where the protective barrier has been removed entirely, making the danger real rather than staged. Hundreds of demons, including hulkers and voiders, swarm up from below toward a rooftop extraction point. Rochelle rejoins and dominates, killing a large flying demon alone and draining a voider mid-attack. Gallant, elated and unstable, defies Erika outright, and Rob, revealing overwhelming power, forcibly subdues and benches him, substituting himself and his subordinate for the team's injured, concussed warder. The floor's true final threat then breaks through: a massive obsidian-armored hulker that reflects essence attacks. With no ranged answer left, Sal fights it hand-to-hand in his transforming armor, sustained by Rochelle's tethered essence, and kills his first hulker with Erika firing his revolver on his call. The team is the first to clear floor five.

Aboard the extraction craft, Prestige confronts Rob for turning the trial into a genuine hulker fight. Rob is revealed as the president of the Hunter Bureau and bearer of the legendary hero name Phantom, and admits he has quietly tracked Sal's crafting for some time; he demands to take Gallant away for a corrective internship and hands personal gala invitations to Sal, Erika, and Rochelle, pointedly excluding Gallant and the team's warder. Quest, once he learns his students cleared five floors, judges Sal, Erika, and Rochelle very likely to become the Academy's first-ever first-year Saviors; Prestige recommends against naming Gallant, and Rochelle refuses to soften her judgment of him. Cleared to go home early, Sal reconnects with the broker Vanessa, reaffirms their guild partnership with proof of his hulker kill, and learns a major secret: the Ark Guild's guildmaster once founded the megastructure whose crew became the antagonist faction Bastion, and Quest Academy itself sits on that project's original launch site. The stretch ends on Sal's sudden alarm at a name Vanessa mentions.

Back at the workshop, Sal reworks a broken crown and obsidian from his hulker kill into a five-attribute circlet he gives Divinity, dramatically amplifying her foresight. Using Perfect deliberately to let her ability pass through him, he is pulled into a vivid vision sixty years ahead: humanity is winning the war and a crafting economy has grown around his own future brand, but a memorial reveals that his mentor Upgrade has died by then. His full stat sheet confirms he has grown stronger and drawn scouting interest from five guilds. At a grand assembly, the Academy names its first fifteen Saviors in reverse rank order; Erika, Rochelle, Barry, and Divinity are all included, Gallant and the team's warder are explicitly excluded, and Sal is revealed as the single top-ranked Savior in the entire Academy, publicly credited for his hulker kill and his crafting. In a final debrief, Quest itemizes Sal's rewards, offers to endorse his guild ambitions to his parents, and confirms a long-dormant outing to a proficiency-holder called Coach. Sal chooses to spend the break at his family's auction house to win his parents' backing in person, and boards the train home with his first semester complete, his guild still unfounded and every major thread carried into the next book.

characters.description: A young Breton lawyer raised as the ward of the Seigneur de Kercadiou, with no certain knowledge of his parents. André-Louis is skeptical, verbally gifted, and initially indifferent to political ideals. The murder of his closest friend drives him to use wit, performance, and eventually the sword against aristocratic privilege.
characters.name: André-Louis Moreau

characters.description: A young seminarian and André-Louis's dearest friend. Vilmorin is an earnest advocate for ordinary people at the opening of the French Revolution and believes that words and moral conviction can challenge inherited power.
characters.name: Philippe de Vilmorin

characters.description: The irascible but affectionate Lord of Gavrillac, godfather and guardian to André-Louis and uncle to Aline. Kercadiou dislikes political agitation and expects personal loyalty to the old social order, yet his household is André's only family.
characters.name: Quintin de Kercadiou

characters.description: Kercadiou's young niece and ward, raised alongside André-Louis at Gavrillac. Intelligent and spirited, Aline understands André better than most people do, though his refusal to speak plainly about his feelings often frustrates her.
characters.name: Aline de Kercadiou

characters.description: A wealthy Breton nobleman, accomplished swordsman, and defender of aristocratic privilege. When Vilmorin challenges the injustice surrounding a peasant's death, La Tour d'Azyr deliberately provokes the inexperienced young man into a duel.
characters.name: Marquis de La Tour d'Azyr

characters.description: A political organizer and spokesman for the Third Estate in Brittany. Le Chapelier recognizes André-Louis's ability to move a crowd and gives practical direction to the anger unleashed by Vilmorin's death.
characters.name: Le Chapelier

characters.description: The manager of a traveling troupe of improvisational players. Binet is practical, vain, protective of his authority, and inclined to measure strangers by how useful they may be to his company.
characters.name: M. Binet

characters.description: Binet's attractive daughter and the leading woman of his troupe. Climène has grown up within the conventions of the traveling stage and is ambitious for both theatrical success and social advancement.
characters.name: Climène Binet

characters.description: An actor in Binet's company who performs the romantic lead. Léandre's place in the established stage pattern helps André-Louis understand both the troupe's stock characters and the opportunities for reshaping their comedy.
characters.name: Léandre

characters.description: A Parisian fencing master whose disciplined teaching reveals a new use for André-Louis's analytical mind. Des Amis treats swordsmanship as a system that can be understood and improved, not merely as an aristocratic accomplishment.
characters.name: Bertrand des Amis

characters.description: A noblewoman and close friend of Aline who takes a strong personal interest in André-Louis during the revolutionary crisis. Her concern for his safety appears unusually intense, though she is cautious about explaining its source.
characters.name: Madame de Plougastel

characters.description: A fashionable noblewoman connected to Aline and Kercadiou. Madame de Sautron encourages the proposed match between Aline and La Tour d'Azyr, viewing the marquis's rank and fortune as decisive advantages.
characters.name: Madame de Sautron

recaps.ending: During the upheaval in Paris, André-Louis gets Aline and Madame de Plougastel away from immediate danger. He learns that Madame de Plougastel is his mother and believes La Tour d'Azyr to be his father, a discovery that makes killing the marquis impossible despite years of hatred. André arranges safe passage out of France for the two older nobles. La Tour d'Azyr departs with Madame de Plougastel, while Kercadiou and Aline remain with André. Aline has rejected the marquis after understanding both his character and André's long devotion to her. André finally drops the emotional masks that have served him as lawyer, agitator, actor, and swordsman. He and Aline acknowledge their love and plan to marry. His revenge is left unfinished, but the man who claimed to have no convictions ends by preserving lives and choosing a future beyond vengeance.
recaps.in_short: Breton lawyer André-Louis Moreau has little interest in politics until the aristocratic Marquis de La Tour d'Azyr kills his idealistic friend Vilmorin in a contrived duel. André becomes Vilmorin's public voice, stirring revolutionary crowds and fleeing the authorities. He hides with traveling actors, transforms their performances, and becomes famous as Scaramouche, but leaves after personal and political conflict destroys the troupe's prospects. In Paris he masters fencing and later enters the National Assembly, where he defeats noble swordsmen who try to intimidate the Third Estate. His private aim remains revenge on La Tour d'Azyr, who is also courting Aline de Kercadiou, the woman André loves. As Paris erupts, André protects Aline and Madame de Plougastel. He learns the latter is his mother and believes the marquis is his father, so he abandons the killing. He helps the older pair escape France and finally admits his love to Aline, who returns it.

recaps.text: In Brittany on the eve of the French Revolution, lawyer André-Louis Moreau lives under the protection of his godfather, Quintin de Kercadiou. His closest friend, Philippe de Vilmorin, is an idealistic seminarian who speaks for peasants abused by noble privilege. When they appeal to the Marquis de La Tour d'Azyr over a peasant's death, the marquis maneuvers Vilmorin into a duel and kills the inexperienced young man. André, previously proud of having no convictions, takes up his friend's cause. He confronts Kercadiou, who refuses to oppose the aristocratic order, then carries the story of Vilmorin's death to the public. His gift for argument turns private grief into political agitation, making both La Tour d'Azyr and the royal authorities his enemies.

Working with leaders of the Third Estate, André speaks in towns across Brittany and becomes the voice of the dead Vilmorin. He does not fully share all the ideals he proclaims, but he knows how to give a crowd language for its anger. His speeches help inflame unrest in Rennes and other towns. Warrants force him to keep moving under assumed identities, while his public attacks on aristocratic privilege make reconciliation with Kercadiou impossible. Pursued by the authorities, André leaves the political platform behind without abandoning either his anger at La Tour d'Azyr or the talents for persuasion that have made him dangerous.

André supplies Binet's players with stronger situations and dialogue, gradually replacing stale improvisation with carefully shaped comedy. Taking the role of Scaramouche, he becomes central to the troupe's success. He and Binet's daughter Climène are drawn together, although her ambition and his secrecy complicate the attachment. As the company rises from provincial performances toward Nantes, André discovers that a theatrical mask can express truths as effectively as a political speech. The troupe's growing fame also makes concealment harder. La Tour d'Azyr enters their orbit and directs attention toward Climène, whose desire for rank makes the nobleman's interest attractive despite André's warnings about his character.

Climène's willingness to accept La Tour d'Azyr's attention breaks André's hopes for their relationship. Political disorder also reaches the theatre, where social tensions and André's past make continued performance impossible. He leaves Binet's company and the identity of Scaramouche behind, though the habits of observation and disguise remain useful. In Paris, André turns to the fencing academy of Bertrand des Amis. He approaches swordsmanship analytically, mastering its principles with unusual speed and helping refine instruction. When des Amis dies, André inherits responsibility for the school. The lawyer and actor has now acquired the skill required to face aristocrats on the ground they have long controlled through training and privilege.

André's reputation as a fencing master grows while France moves toward open revolution. He reconnects with political allies and enters the National Assembly as a representative of the Third Estate. Noble deputies attempt to frighten reformers through challenges and duels, but André answers them with the expertise acquired at the academy, defeating a succession of aristocratic swordsmen. His public campaign advances the political struggle and brings him closer to his private target, La Tour d'Azyr. At the same time, the marquis is being promoted as a husband for Aline. André opposes the match but still conceals the depth of his own love for her. Madame de Plougastel, Aline's friend, shows an unexplained concern for André and urges caution as his pursuit of vengeance becomes more dangerous.

Revolutionary violence spreads through Paris, endangering nobles regardless of their individual conduct. André's anger at privilege does not make him willing to surrender Aline or Madame de Plougastel to a mob, and he uses his political standing, nerve, and skill to protect them. His long conflict with La Tour d'Azyr approaches its conclusion, but Madame de Plougastel's intense fear for both men reveals that the struggle is bound to André's unknown parentage. André learns that she is the mother who gave him up and comes to believe that La Tour d'Azyr is his father. The discovery transforms revenge into a moral and personal crisis: killing the man he has pursued would also mean knowingly killing his own parent.

André abandons his plan to kill La Tour d'Azyr and uses his influence to arrange safe passage from revolutionary France for the threatened nobles. Madame de Plougastel leaves with the marquis, while Kercadiou and Aline remain. Aline no longer intends to marry La Tour d'Azyr and understands that André's opposition arose from love as well as hatred. Having survived as advocate, fugitive, Scaramouche, fencing master, and deputy, André finally speaks without a public role or disguise. He and Aline declare their love and look toward marriage. Vilmorin's death has not been avenged in the simple form André once sought, but it has driven him into the revolutionary cause and through the discovery of his own family. He ends by choosing mercy and a shared future over the identity built around vengeance.

characters.description: An eighteen-year-old farmer from Rieux in southern France, who runs her grandmother's produce farm and flies the deliveries into Toulouse herself in a battered old ship. Blunt, quick-tempered and fiercely loyal, she has spent two weeks fighting the police, who have written off her grandmother's disappearance as a woman walking out on her life rather than an abduction. She wears a red hooded sweatshirt, waits tables at the village tavern when money is short, and carries her grandmother's gun.
characters.name: Scarlet Benoit

characters.description: Scarlet's grandmother and the woman who raised her, a retired military pilot who ran the farm outside Rieux alone for decades. She vanished two weeks before the book opens without a message, a packed bag or any sign of struggle the police will accept. Scarlet is certain she was taken, and equally certain her grandmother was hiding something for most of her life.
characters.name: Michelle Benoit

characters.description: A waitress at the Rieux tavern and a friend of Scarlet's, cheerfully fascinated by the newcomer fighting in the tavern's back room.
characters.name: Émilie

characters.description: A street fighter who turned up in Rieux a few weeks ago and wins in the tavern's back room without apparent effort. Tall and heavily built, with unruly hair, green eyes and a tattoo of letters and numbers on his forearm, he is unnervingly fast in the ring and awkward and quiet outside it. He pays more attention to Scarlet's missing grandmother than a drifter passing through a village has any reason to.
characters.name: Wolf

characters.description: The cyborg mechanic from New Beijing, now the most wanted fugitive on Earth, sitting in a prison cell awaiting delivery to Luna. She knows at last what she is, Lunar and the missing Princess Selene, and wears the improved cyborg hand and foot Dr. Erland left her, but she has no plan beyond getting out of the building.
characters.name: Linh Cinder

characters.description: An American cadet turned thief held in the same New Beijing prison as Cinder, jailed for stealing a military spaceship. Talkative, vain and relentlessly pleased with himself, he offers Cinder a way off the planet on the grounds that the stolen ship is still exactly where he left it.
characters.name: Carswell Thorne

characters.description: The newly crowned emperor of the Eastern Commonwealth, negotiating with Queen Levana while the plague spreads and his own people demand the escaped cyborg be recaptured. Publicly he is the ruler who was deceived by a Lunar fugitive; privately he cannot decide what he believes about her.
characters.name: Emperor Kai

characters.description: The queen of Luna, waiting on the moon for the marriage that will make her empress of the Eastern Commonwealth, and using the promise of the plague antidote to force the pace. She wants the escaped cyborg returned above everything else, and will not say why.
characters.name: Queen Levana

characters.description: The palace scientist who told Cinder what she is and then vanished from New Beijing, leaving her an address in Africa and instructions to find him there. He is absent for most of the book, but everything Cinder does is aimed at eventually reaching him.
characters.name: Dr. Dmitri Erland

characters.description: Scarlet's estranged father, who drank his way out of her childhood and reappears at the farmhouse burned and badly frightened. He was seized by the same men who took Michelle, held while they tried to get information out of him that he did not have, and let go.
characters.name: Luc Benoit

characters.description: Levana's head thaumaturge, running the queen's operations on Earth from the pack's base in Paris. Composed and unhurried, she treats Earthens and her own subordinates alike as instruments, and what she wants is everything Michelle Benoit knows.
characters.name: Sybil Mira

characters.description: One of the Lunar operatives quartered in Paris, and Wolf's younger brother. Taken as a child in the same conscription, he has spent years trying to prove himself to their handlers and resents everything about the brother who left.
characters.name: Ran Kesley

characters.description: Cinder's dismantled android friend, reduced to a personality chip that Cinder carried out of New Beijing in her pocket. Aboard the stolen ship she is given somewhere to live again, and immediately has opinions about it.
characters.name: Iko

recaps.ending: Michelle Benoit is killed in the Paris opera house after confirming what she spent her life protecting: she sheltered the injured Lunar princess Selene on her farm for years and arranged the new identity that placed her with a family in New Beijing. That gives Cinder independent proof of who she is. Wolf breaks with his pack to protect Scarlet and is badly hurt doing it, and Sybil Mira escapes with the information she extracted. Cinder, Thorne, Scarlet and Wolf leave Earth together aboard the Rampion, now crewed by Iko, whose personality chip Cinder installs in the ship's systems. Wolf explains that the Paris pack was one of many: Lunar soldiers have been quietly moved into cities across the planet for years, waiting for an order. Emperor Kai publicly announces his engagement to Queen Levana in exchange for the plague antidote, and within hours of the broadcast the packs attack cities on every continent and the invasion of Earth begins. Cinder sets course for Africa to find Dr. Erland, having decided she will not keep running: she means to stop the wedding and claim the Lunar throne herself.
recaps.in_short: Cinder breaks out of the New Beijing prison with a charming thief named Carswell Thorne and escapes Earth aboard his stolen ship, the Rampion, chasing a name from her own past: Michelle Benoit. In France, Michelle's granddaughter Scarlet is fighting to find the woman herself, who vanished without trace. Scarlet falls in with Wolf, a street fighter who turns out to be a Lunar special operative rebuilt around wolf DNA, and who leads her to the pack holding her grandmother in a Paris opera house. There Michelle reveals that she hid the injured Lunar princess Selene on her farm for years before arranging her new life in New Beijing, and is then killed in front of Scarlet. Wolf turns on his own pack to protect Scarlet, and Cinder arrives in time to fight the thaumaturge running the operation. The four escape together on the Rampion with Iko installed as the ship. Kai announces his engagement to Levana, and Luna's soldiers, planted in cities across Earth, begin the invasion.

recaps.text: Previously: Linh Cinder, a cyborg mechanic in New Beijing, was conscripted for plague research and found to be immune to letumosis, then learned the reason - she is Lunar, one of the moon colony's people, who can control what others perceive. Queen Levana of Luna came to Earth demanding marriage to the young emperor Kai in exchange for the plague antidote, meaning to take the Commonwealth and dispose of him afterwards. Cinder went to the royal ball to warn him, was exposed in front of the court as both cyborg and Lunar, and was imprisoned. There the palace scientist Dr. Erland, a Lunar defector himself, told her the truth: she is Princess Selene, the Lunar heir believed to have died in a nursery fire as a small child, smuggled to Earth, rebuilt as a cyborg and hidden ever since. She is the only legitimate rival to Levana's throne. Kai agreed to the marriage to buy the antidote for his dying people, and Cinder was to be handed over to Luna for execution. Her stepsister Peony died of the plague, her android friend Iko was dismantled, and Erland left her a stronger cyborg hand, an escape plan and an address in Africa.

In Rieux, a farming village in southern France, eighteen-year-old Scarlet Benoit has spent two weeks trying to make the police look for her grandmother, Michelle, who disappeared without a word. They close the case as a voluntary departure. At the tavern where Scarlet waits tables she meets a newcomer called Wolf, a street fighter with a tattoo of letters and numbers on his forearm, unnervingly strong in the ring and awkward outside it. In New Beijing, Cinder waits in prison for transfer to Luna and uses her untrained Lunar gift on a guard to get out of her cell. She finds another prisoner, Carswell Thorne, an American cadet jailed for stealing a military spaceship, who offers her a way off the planet if she takes him with her.

Cinder and Thorne escape New Beijing aboard the Rampion, the stolen ship Thorne had hidden, and go into hiding while the Commonwealth broadcasts Cinder's face across Earth. In France, Scarlet's estranged father turns up at the farmhouse burned and terrified: he was seized by the same men who took Michelle, who wanted something Michelle had hidden years ago and would not give up. Wolf admits he recognises them - Lunar operatives working out of Paris - and offers to take Scarlet to where they are. With no better option, she agrees, and the two set off north.

Scarlet and Wolf travel toward Paris by train. In pieces, Wolf tells her what he is: taken from his family as a boy and rebuilt by Luna into a special operative, surgically and genetically fused with wolf DNA, trained in packs, and that he ran away from it. Scarlet does not know how much of it to believe. Cinder, hunting anything that explains her own past, follows a name out of the royal android's data - Michelle Benoit, a retired French pilot with an unexplained gap in her military record - and brings the Rampion down in Europe. On Earth, Kai negotiates with Levana over the antidote and the wedding while being pressed publicly to recapture the escaped cyborg.

Wolf takes Scarlet into Paris, where the pack has occupied the old opera house, and there she learns his loyalties were never what he claimed: he was sent to find her, and the journey north was a delivery. Scarlet is taken prisoner in the cellars. Cinder and Thorne reach the Benoit farm, find it abandoned and search it, then follow the trail toward Paris. Levana's head thaumaturge Sybil Mira is running the operation, and what she wants is everything Michelle Benoit knew about a child she once hid.

In the opera house cellars Scarlet is reunited with her grandmother, who has been held and questioned for weeks and has given up nothing. Michelle finally explains what she was protecting. Years ago a Lunar doctor brought her a badly burned Lunar child to hide, and she kept the girl in a suspended-animation tank in the farm's barn until she was old enough to be given a new identity and placed with a family on the other side of the world. The child was Princess Selene. Michelle destroyed every record and shrank her own life down to the farm rather than risk being traced. Scarlet realises her grandmother's disappearance was never about the two of them at all.

Sybil Mira gets what she came for and has Michelle killed in front of Scarlet. Wolf, who has been playing the obedient operative in front of his pack, breaks with them to protect Scarlet and is beaten for it. Cinder and Thorne reach the opera house and find the pack quartered inside. Cinder confronts Sybil directly and discovers that her untrained gift is strong enough to stand against a trained thaumaturge.

The fight spreads through the opera house. Wolf turns on the pack outright, including his younger brother Ran, who has spent years trying to prove himself to their handlers. Cinder uses her gift on the wolf soldiers to break the pack's discipline, Thorne fights his way clear, and Scarlet gets out of the cellars. Sybil escapes with what she took from Michelle. Wolf is left badly injured and, for the first time in his life, on no one's side but Scarlet's.

Cinder, Thorne, Scarlet and Wolf escape Paris aboard the Rampion. Cinder installs Iko's salvaged personality chip in the ship, giving the android a voice and a body of sorts again. Scarlet has lost her grandmother but has confirmation of what Michelle died protecting, and Cinder has proof of her own history from someone other than Dr. Erland. Wolf tells them what the pack was for: hundreds of Lunar soldiers have been placed in cities across Earth over the past years, and Paris held only one of them. On Earth, Kai announces his engagement to Queen Levana, and within hours the wolf soldiers rise in cities on every continent. The crew sets course for Africa to find Erland, with Cinder resolved to stop the wedding and take the throne she was born to.
